rows.text: Galadriel is strongest when you make creatures enter during EVERY player's turn. Her three modes are available again each turn, so do not spend your entire hand in your own main phase and pass with nothing to do. This is a creature-and-token engine backed by blink interaction, with combat finishers that turn accumulated resources into a win.

guide.title: Make the commander work all round

rows.name: Galadriel, Light of Valinor
rows.text: choose the mode as each trigger goes onto the stack, not when it resolves. Each mode can be chosen once per turn for that particular Galadriel. Extra creature entrances after all three choices are used give no further benefit unless you blink her to reset her.

The mana mode is a triggered ability that uses the stack. It cannot help pay for the creature that triggered it, and unused mana disappears as steps and phases end. If several creatures enter together, you still choose different modes for their triggers; three tokens do not make nine green mana.

rows.name: Seedborn Muse
rows.text: refreshes your lands, mana creatures, and artifacts on every opponent's untap step. Spend that mana on blink, flash creatures, and interaction. Untapping a newly cast creature does not remove summoning sickness.

rows.name: Emiel the Blessed + Galadriel, Light of Valinor
rows.text: pay three to blink a useful OTHER creature, then Galadriel's unused mana mode can refund three green mana. Blinking Galadriel herself resets her choices but does not trigger her own alliance ability; you still need another creature to enter afterward.

rows.name: Whitemane Lion
rows.text: flash it in and return itself to hand to get a repeatable entrance without losing a card. One cast can save a threatened creature instead. Galadriel's green mana does not pay the white pip of the next Lion, so keep white sources available.

rows.name: Alchemist's Refuge + Winding Canyons
rows.text: convert spare mana into flash access. Refuge permits all spells for the turn; Canyons permits only creatures. Activate before committing the spells, and remember each activation also taps the land.

rows.name: Tendershoot Dryad + Wolverine Riders
rows.text: each creates a creature on EVERY upkeep. Use those entrances for cards when your hand is weak, counters when developing lethal combat, or mana only when you have an instant-speed use during that upkeep. Riders also supplies life as your Elves enter.

rows.name: The Queen of Dale
rows.text: opponents' first noncreature spells each turn let you draw then discard. Discarding a nonland card creates a Soldier, which can trigger Galadriel and Aura Shards. This filters rather than increasing your hand size by itself.

rows.name: Koma, Cosmos Serpent
rows.text: a large independent threat that makes a 3/3 every upkeep. Coils protect Koma from destruction or tap a blocker and stop its activated abilities for the turn. Avoid tapping down lands as a recurring denial plan; the deck is built for Bracket 3 combat.

guide.title: Reuse the best creature on the battlefield

rows.name: Soulherder + Thassa, Deep-Dwelling
rows.text: provide free end-step blinks of your removal, tutor, or draw creatures. Each triggers only at the beginning of YOUR end step. If Galadriel has already used every mode, the creature's own entrance effect is still valuable.

rows.name: Ephemerate
rows.text: one white mana protects a creature from targeted removal and reuses its entrance, then rebound can do it again next upkeep. It does not save a creature from a sweeper still waiting on the stack: the creature returns before that sweeper resolves.

rows.name: Restoration Angel
rows.text: flash plus a second entrance makes two Galadriel triggers if she stays in play. Blink a non-Angel value creature or save one from targeted removal. She cannot blink herself.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines
rows.text: doubles your creature entrance triggers, including Aura Shards and Galadriel, while disabling opponents' entrance-trigger engines. Galadriel still chooses different unused modes; the double trigger does not let you pick mana twice.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker
rows.text: turn an expendable card into the creature the current position needs, then reuse that search by blinking it. Its tap ability can untap a mana creature or utility land; it needs to be free of summoning sickness to use that ability.

rows.name: Eternal Witness
rows.text: recovers a spent tutor, protection spell, or finisher. Blink it when you have a specific card to recover, rather than automatically resetting a counter-covered attacker.

rows.name: Sevinne's Reclamation
rows.text: rebuilds cheap foundations such as Aura Shards, The Queen of Dale, Soulherder, or a land. Flashback can return two permanents. It cannot recover Galadriel, Emiel, or Seedborn Muse.

Blinking removes counters and makes a creature a new object with summoning sickness. Do not blink your largest attacker before combat unless you can restore haste or the entrance effect is worth the lost attack. Exiled creature tokens cannot return.

guide.title: Reach five mana without falling behind

rows.name: Birds of Paradise + Noble Hierarch + Avacyn's Pilgrim
rows.text: one-mana acceleration supplies the white and blue needed for Galadriel while leaving more lands untapped on later turns. These creatures become real attackers after counter triggers and a finisher.

rows.name: Llanowar Elves + Elvish Mystic
rows.text: more turn-one ramp so you can develop an engine before casting your five-mana commander. Their green-only output makes the dual-land manabase important.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: protects Galadriel and your other legendary spells from counterspells when you spend its colored mana on them. Its colored mode cannot cast ordinary creatures or interaction.

rows.name: Bloom Tender + Galadriel, Light of Valinor
rows.text: Galadriel supplies all three colors, making Tender tap for green, white, and blue. This fixes the colored pips that Galadriel's own three-green trigger cannot cover.

rows.name: Badgermole Cub
rows.text: earthbends a land into a hasty creature and adds green when you tap a creature for mana, including your mana creatures and that animated land. Animating an existing land does not make a creature enter, so earthbend itself does not provide an extra alliance trigger.

rows.name: Enduring Vitality
rows.text: turns every established creature into a mana source of any color. It returns as a noncreature enchantment after dying, making it useful after destruction wipes. New tokens still have summoning sickness.

rows.name: Springleaf Parade
rows.text: builds multiple bodies and turns creature tokens into colored mana sources. X=3 can supply all three alliance choices if unused, but those tokens cannot immediately tap for mana without haste. The mana ability also works on your other token types.

rows.name: Sol Ring + Arcane Signet
rows.text: early acceleration and later resources that Seedborn Muse untaps. Ring pays generic blink and spell costs; Signet supplies any of your three colors.

rows.name: Nature's Lore + Three Visits
rows.text: find typed dual lands, usually an untapped source that completes your colors. Original duals and shocklands are Forest cards where printed; you are not limited to the single basic Forest.

rows.name: The Great Henge
rows.text: counter growth reduces its casting cost, and nontoken entrances draw cards while adding more counters. It is not a two-mana spell by default; evaluate the strongest creature you actually control before keeping an opening hand around it.

guide.title: Keep drawing even if Galadriel is removed

rows.name: Danny Pink + Galadriel, Light of Valinor
rows.text: Galadriel's team-counter mode can draw one card for every creature receiving its first counters that turn while Danny grants the ability. Repeat on opponents' turns to refill rapidly; additional counters on the same creature that turn do not draw again.

rows.name: Danny Pink + The Great Henge
rows.text: a nontoken creature entering can draw from Henge and from receiving its first counter that turn. If you later choose Galadriel's counter mode, that creature has already used its Danny draw for the turn.

rows.name: Guardian Project
rows.text: nontoken creatures and their repeated blink entrances draw cards without relying on the commander. Token production does not trigger it, and its same-name checks still matter if opponents copy or return your cards.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: counters increase the tax on opponents' first noncreature spell each turn, improving the chance of drawing as the game progresses. It is not a trigger for every spell.

rows.name: Mystic Remora + Faerie Mastermind
rows.text: efficient independent draw against spell-heavy and card-draw-heavy opponents. Do not pay Remora's upkeep indefinitely if it prevents developing mana; Mastermind's flash also enables alliance on another player's turn.

rows.name: Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar
rows.text: shuts off opponents' spells during YOUR turn, helping your finishers resolve. Creatures raised above base power by counters can draw on connecting with different players. Opponents can still use activated and triggered abilities.

guide.title: Answers that also advance the engine

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: every creature entrance, including tokens, becomes optional artifact or enchantment removal. Hold instant-speed entrances when an opponent may present an important engine. It is powerful enough to draw removal, so do not rely on it as your only answer.

rows.name: Chomping Changeling
rows.text: an artifact/enchantment answer on a body you can tutor and blink. Its destruction is optional, so you can cast it into an empty opposing board without destroying your own engine.

rows.name: Skyclave Apparition
rows.text: exiles a cheap nontoken permanent permanently. When Apparition leaves, that card does not return; its owner instead receives an Illusion token. Repeated blinking accumulates removal but can leave substantial opposing blockers.

rows.name: Solitude + Ephemerate
rows.text: evoke Solitude, then blink it before its sacrifice trigger resolves. The returned Solitude is a new object that stays, and its removal triggers again. You still paid for evoke by exiling a white card.

rows.name: Endurance
rows.text: flash graveyard disruption on a useful blocker. It puts the targeted graveyard under its owner's library rather than exiling it. Evoke and blink can also preserve this creature while generating another entrance.

rows.name: Mystic Snake + Emiel the Blessed
rows.text: with a spell on the stack, three mana can blink Snake to counter it. This is repeatable interaction limited by available mana, not a hard lock; opponents can respond and force competing demands on your resources.

rows.name: Venser, Shaper Savant
rows.text: returns a spell or permanent to hand, letting you answer an uncounterable spell or temporarily remove a problematic permanent. Prefer nonland targets; this is not a repeated land-bounce strategy.

rows.name: Aang, Swift Savior
rows.text: a three-mana flash answer to a creature or a spell. Airbending lets its OWNER cast it from exile for two mana later, so use it to stop a critical play or save your own creature with a plan to recast. It is not permanent exile.

rows.name: Riptide Gearhulk
rows.text: can bury one nonland permanent from EACH opponent third from the top, keeping you from spending three separate removal spells. Blink it for another batch; opponents may redraw the cards later.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares + Beast Within
rows.text: efficient answers when you need a response immediately. Beast Within covers troublesome permanent types your creature-exile spells miss, at the cost of giving a 3/3.

rows.name: Mana Drain + Swan Song + Dovin's Veto
rows.text: protect the board from sweepers and stop dangerous noncreature engines or wins. Mana Drain also counters creatures and can fund a later blink or finisher; Veto cannot counter a creature spell.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift + Winds of Abandon
rows.text: scalable one-sided resets that can also open a lethal attack. Overloaded Winds gives opponents basic lands, so use it to stabilize a dangerous board or finish promptly rather than handing out ramp casually.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: protects your permanents from most targeted removal and destruction. It does not stop sacrifice, mass exile, or a sufficiently large toughness reduction.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: convoke your creatures to phase out your important nonland permanents against a sweeper, including exile. Lands remain exposed. A newly cast creature can convoke even though it cannot tap for a mana ability.

rows.name: Galadriel's Dismissal
rows.text: one mana phases out a threatened creature; kicked, it can save your entire creature board or remove one opponent's blockers. It does not protect your standalone artifacts and enchantments.

rows.name: March of Swirling Mist
rows.text: protects a selected group or phases out blockers across multiple opponents. Exiling blue cards reduces generic costs only; you still choose X and must pay the blue mana.

Phasing is different from blink: it preserves counters and does not cause entrance triggers. Phased-out permanents normally return before their controller untaps, so phasing your own established army does not give it summoning sickness.

guide.title: Convert resources into a decisive attack

rows.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: the principal tutorable combat finish. Count creatures and available attackers separately: new tokens increase the bonus, but normally cannot attack. Craterhoof gives trample and a power boost, but only Craterhoof itself has innate haste.

rows.name: Moonshaker Cavalry
rows.text: a second tutorable team pump with flying. It supplies no haste, including for itself, so use an established army or Finale's haste effect.

rows.name: Finale of Devastation -> Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: X=8 finds Hoof for ten total mana; X=10 costs twelve and also gives the whole team +10/+10 and haste. Search the graveyard when Hoof has already died.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with your commander present, flying, double strike, lifelink, indestructible, and protection from each color turn a counter-grown army into a fast kill. Without a commander you choose one mode, and the spell itself does not add power.

rows.name: Emiel the Blessed + Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: blink Hoof in your precombat main phase for an additional team pump before declaring attackers. Count your attackers and mana first; this is a finite combat burst, not an infinite combo.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift + Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar
rows.text: on your own turn, Kutzil stops opponents casting spells while you clear blockers and commit a finisher. Activated abilities, triggered abilities, and effects already on the battlefield remain relevant.

rows.name: Eladamri's Call -> Seedborn Muse
rows.text: find Muse when Emiel, a flash land, or several flash creatures already give you ways to spend mana each turn. Call puts the creature into your hand, not onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Chord of Calling -> Emiel the Blessed
rows.text: convoke out the repeatable blink engine when you already have profitable targets and mana to activate it. Chord's own cost does not include the activation mana.

rows.name: Chord of Calling -> Solitude
rows.text: find immediate creature exile at instant speed; a creature put onto the battlefield this way is not evoked and is not sacrificed for evoke.

rows.name: Green Sun's Zenith -> Tendershoot Dryad
rows.text: establish an every-upkeep token engine when your board is thin. Zenith finds only green creatures, so it cannot find Emiel, Solitude, or Moonshaker Cavalry.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker -> Danny Pink
rows.text: find the draw engine when you already have a team and can generate a Galadriel counter trigger. You must discard a card to perform Speaker's search.

rows.name: Formidable Speaker -> Moonshaker Cavalry
rows.text: when flying will close a board stall and you can pay the triple-white casting cost, find the finishing creature rather than another value engine.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand and how to sequence

rows.text: Keep three lands or a credible two-land-plus-ramp hand, early acceleration, and either a draw engine or interaction. Prioritize access to all three colors by the time you want Galadriel. A hand full of expensive blink targets and finishers needs a mulligan even if every card is individually strong.

Use a turn-one mana creature and a turn-two ramp or draw play to aim for Galadriel around turns three through four on a good hand. Do not cast her into obvious removal with no follow-up when developing another engine would be better.

Fetch untapped duals when you need your mana now; fetch a surveil land or Spara's Headquarters when the tapped land will not cost you a play. The three basics are utility/search protection targets, not the core color-fixing plan.

Once Galadriel is established, decide which modes matter BEFORE making creatures enter. Take green mana only when you can use it in the current step, take cards when rebuilding, and take counters before combat or with Danny Pink. You do not need to use all three modes every turn to be ahead.

Avoid overcommitting into a sweeper: an independent draw source, one repeatable entrance engine, and protection are often enough. Save a token maker or recursion spell for the rebuild rather than emptying the hand.

This list aims to win with a developed board around turns six through eight; that is an estimate, not a guaranteed clock. It has no designed infinite combo, extra-turn chain, or mass land denial. Combat needs real attackers, and losing Galadriel slows the engine without removing the deck's draw, token, or finisher plans.
